key_insight: Combining scaled boundary finite elements with an FFT-based solver enables stable, matrix-free elastic homogenization of porous and highly heterogeneous voxel microstructures.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers an alternative to overly stiff fully integrated voxel elements and potentially unstable reduced-integration elements for composites and porous materials.
method: Discretize a periodic voxel grid with hexahedral SBFEM cells using analytical radial solutions.
Apply a homogeneous SBFEM preconditioner locally in Fourier space without assembling the global stiffness matrix.
Bound the preconditioned condition number by material contrast, independently of grid resolution.
evidence_signal: Tests on a short-fibre composite, polyurethane foam and sand-based binder jet microstructure showed robust convergence and competitive accuracy, including stability in porous cases where reduced-integration elements became unstable.
watch_item: The demonstrated scope is three-dimensional linear elasticity on regular periodic voxel grids; nonlinear and nonperiodic applications are not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Scaled boundary finite elements for FFT-based computational micromechanics
